reason: Grouping fibres seems like the first step toward building a muscle that can pull on the arm.
expectation: I expect a bundle of muscle fibres, though it may still need connective tissue to form a muscle.

alternatives.reason: Blood vessels should support the arm, but grouping fibres seems more directly related to the goal.

effect: The fibres formed a bundle, so adding connective tissue looks like the next step toward a muscle.
reaction: The paired poses help connect the bundle to the shortening fibre, though the result was expected.
reason: The sheaths appear to organize and support the fibre bundle as part of a muscle.
expectation: I expect a wrapped muscle bundle or a more complete muscle.

alternatives.reason: The blood vessels may support the arm, but I want to finish building the muscle first.

effect: The bundle and sheaths formed a biceps with tendons, explaining how the fibres' pull reaches the bones and why an opposing muscle is needed.
reaction: The connection between sheaths, tendons and elbow movement is clear; I didn't expect the biceps to be attached already.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and appears to build up the arm.
expectation: I expect an arm skeleton supplied with blood vessels; I'm unsure how that will lead to attaching the opposing muscles.

effect: The blood vessels produced an arm assembly with slots for the opposing muscles, making the next steps clear.
reaction: The slots clarify the goal, though I didn't expect adding blood vessels to create the assembly.
reason: I'll fit the biceps first because I just built it and it should fill the flexor slot.
expectation: I expect the biceps to occupy the flexor slot, leaving the extensor slot for the triceps.

alternatives.reason: The triceps should fill the opposing slot, but either muscle seems reasonable to add first.

effect: The biceps is fitted, leaving the triceps as the next available muscle to add.
reaction: The fitting was expected and straightforward.
reason: The triceps should complete the opposing muscle pair at the elbow.
expectation: I expect the triceps to fill the extensor slot and complete the opposing muscles.

effect: The triceps is fitted alongside the biceps; the arm still needs the shoulder and hand tissues.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though no goal completion was announced yet.
reason: Adding the remaining tissues is the only offered combination and should complete the arm.
expectation: I expect a more complete arm and possibly completion of the goal.

effect: Adding the shoulder and hand tissues completed the supplied moving arm and the chapter goal.
reaction: The completion was expected, though the final picture mainly brings the parts together without explaining more about their roles.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the biceps with tendons was most worthwhile: it connected the fibre bundle to bone movement and explained why an opposing muscle is needed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the two muscles felt repetitive because each produced only a fitting message, with no further explanation of movement.

surprise.text: I was surprised that adding blood vessels created an arm assembly with muscle slots; the result made the next actions clearer.

arbitrary.text: The blood-vessel combination's immediate purpose was unclear before it produced the arm assembly. Adding the shoulder and hand tissues was also required for the goal, but their contribution was not explained.

continue.text: I might continue for another chapter to see how the moving arm connects to other body systems, though the mostly predetermined fittings made this chapter less engaging.
